test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 6 Oct 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to take the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts and decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All Buildings are Cements.

All Cements are Powders.

All Powders are Detergents.

**Conclusions:**

(I) All Powders are Buildings.

(II) Some Detergents are Cements.
solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6d1ef5eb5386d85461bb698e8dcd2c65b04a71d4d1d26be180d5f5044331087c.png] 

Conclusions:

(I) All Powders are Buildings → Does not follow (As all Buildings are Cements and all Cements are Powders. So it is possible but not definite.)

(II) Some Detergents are Cements → Follow (As all Cements are Powders and all Powders are Detergents. As whole cements comes in powders which whole comes in detergents, therefore it is true.)

∴ Here, Only conclusion (II) follows.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".
